title: Sort Algorithm Visualizer
description: Build a sorting visualizer that generates random arrays, implements bubble and selection sort, and compares their performance.

steps.description: Write a `generateArray` function that takes a `size` parameter and returns an array of random integers between 1 and 100. Log the generated array.
hints: Create an array of the given size using a loop or Array.from()
Log: 'Generated array of size ' + size + ': ' + JSON.stringify(arr)

steps.title: Implement bubble sort
steps.description: Write a `bubbleSort` function that sorts an array in place using the bubble sort algorithm. Return the sorted array and log the result.
hints: Use nested loops: outer loop from i = 0 to n-1, inner from j = 0 to n-i-1

codeTemplate.python:

sorted = bubbleSort(arr.copy())

steps.description: Modify your bubble sort to track and return the number of `comparisons` and `swaps` performed. Log the stats after sorting.
hints: Initialize counters: let comparisons = 0; let swaps = 0;
Increment comparisons each time you compare two elements
Increment swaps each time you swap two elements

steps.title: Compare algorithm performance
steps.description: Write a `compareSorts` function that generates a random array, sorts it with both algorithms, and returns an object with the time and stats for each. Log the comparison.
hints: Generate a random array of size 50 using generateArray
Run bubbleSortWithStats on a copy, run selectionSort on another copy
Use performance.now() or time.time() to measure execution time
Return and log: { bubble: { time, comparisons, swaps }, selection: { time, comparisons, swaps } }

verification.successMessage: Algorithm comparison shows stats for both bubble sort and selection sort!
verification.failureMessage: compareSorts should return stats for both algorithms run on the same random array of size 50.
